content.comment_body: Is it possible to use a web server as a network input on [article_no]?
Yes, it is possible. However, you cannot send a single bit directly; you must use a bit pattern within a byte, word, or dword.

I’ve attached an illustration of how I managed to control a function with the web server. This setting can be accessed through both the front panel display/keys and the web server. It allows you to enable 'holiday mode' for your system, so the tanks and pipes stay warm without production control, which is useful when the operator is away. To set this up, add a soft key to your [product_name] FBD and connect its output to whatever needs changing when the key is on (see first part of the illustration). Next, create a Message Text block including the soft key, ensuring protection is disabled and the web server option is selected (shown in the middle image). Once displayed, the message can be edited from both the local display and the web server (final image). This setup is quite helpful for remote activation of holiday mode if someone forgets to set it before leaving.
Thanks for your replies. I am an embedded engineer and new to [product_name] programming. I want to control home devices from my phone or PC and that's why I asked.
A new question posted by [user_name] has been moved to a different thread titled Book or reference to learn [product_name] programming? Best regards [user_name]

The user indicated little experience with [product_name] programming, signaling a need for more accessible beginner documentation.
